spec.description: Text products issued in a span of time, newest first, narrowed by type, office, location or WMO heading. Header fields only; `products.get_product` fetches one with its text.

request.title: ListProductsRequest
request.description: Which products. Every filter is optional. Give one value per array filter: the service reads several only comma-separated, and this client sends them as repeated keys, of which the service keeps the last.

location.description: Issuance locations to narrow to, such as `SEW`.

start.description: Start of the span, inclusive. The service keeps about a week of products here; an older start returns nothing rather than failing.

end.description: End of the span, exclusive: a product issued at exactly `end` is not returned.

office.description: Four-letter issuing offices to narrow to, such as `KSEW`.

wmoid.description: WMO abbreviated headings to narrow to, four letters and two digits, such as `FXUS66`.

type.description: Three-letter product types to narrow to, such as `AFD`. Left un-enumerated: `products.list_product_types` lists over 300 codes, and the service adds them.

limit.description: Products per response. Range [1, 500]; the service refuses anything outside it with a 400. Without it the service answers up to 5000.

response.description: The products, newest first, without their text.

notes: No `pagination` block, deliberately. The service truncates a span to its newest `limit` products and hands back no cursor, so the only walk is a `seek` that moves `end` to the oldest `issuanceTime` of each full page. Measured 2026-09-30 with `type=AFD`: `end=2026-09-29T05:59:00Z` returned nothing issued at 05:59, and `start=05:52&end=05:59` returned the 05:52 rows and not the 05:59 ones, so `end` is exclusive and `start` inclusive. `issuanceTime` has minute resolution and is not unique (the unfiltered first page held 5000 products over 31 minutes, about 160 a minute). A walk that moved an exclusive `end` to a shared minute would skip that minute's unread products, so no walk is declared rather than a lossy one.

The service reads an array filter comma-separated (the OpenAPI declares `explode: false`), and keeps only the last of repeated keys. Measured 2026-09-30: `type=AFD&type=TOR` returns only TOR products, `type=AFD,TOR` returns both. This client's core sends repeated keys, as it does for every other array filter in this API, so until the core joins them only the last value of each filter takes effect. The example sends one value per filter.
